originality.rationale: The reviewed claim is the conditional variance of the total crossing count and its sharp arc maximum. Original Flajolet–Noy section 2 gives only unconditional crossing moments; Acan section 2 gives only the distinguished chord degree moments. Neither provides their mixed covariance, which is a separately computed positive structural term. The first conditional mean is explicitly treated as prior-implied. Closest retrieved research records concern a generic-chord orbit count or geometric polygon chords rather than a uniform perfect matching. Historical priority of the variance formula is provisional, and a plausible generating-function paper remains abstract-only.
residual_risks: Historical or later two-variable generating functions for rooted matchings may indirectly encode this conditional variance.
Pilaud–Rué full text was not inspected; no full-document noncoverage claim is made.
Research-record search and finite enumeration do not constitute proof of universal priority.

value.rationale: The natural global crossing-count variance of a random chord diagram responds nontrivially to conditioning on one root chord. The exact positive mixed covariance is invisible to existing separate global crossing and root-degree moment formulas; the result gives a sharp shape-dependent variance inflation and a complete zero/maximum classification, with order-n^2 maximal effect. No additional theorem outside this natural invariant is needed for its precise usefulness.
